paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption_used: The effect of context masking on case tasks grouped by language family, with error bars indicating standard deviation. Six model configurations are compared across nine language families: mBERT-L2, XLM-L2, mBERT-R2, XLM-R2, mBERT-B2, and XLM-B2. The IE-Indic family shows the largest effects overall, with most configurations reaching between 17 and 25, while Uralic and Isolate families show near-zero effects across all models. Notably, IE-Germanic exhibits consistently higher effects than IE-Romance across all configurations, with XLM-B2 reaching approximately 20 in IE-Germanic. The Semitic family displays the widest error bars overall, suggesting high variability, and the mBERT-L2 bars in Semitic reach approximately 15. In IE-Slavic, the B2 variants (mBERT-B2 and XLM-B2) dominate over the L2 and R2 variants, with effects approximately twice as large.
model_annotation: The chart illustrates the measured “effect” of context masking on case-related tasks across language families, with six model configurations shown side by side for each family and vertical error bars indicating variability (standard deviation). The horizontal axis contains the categorical language-family groups in the following left-to-right order: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis is labeled “effect” and uses a linear scale with labeled ticks at 0, 10, 20, and 30, spanning roughly from slightly below 0 (to accommodate small negative bars) up to the mid-30s. Within each language-family group, six adjacent bars appear in a consistent legend order and color scheme: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light pink), and XLM-B₂ (red). Approximate bar heights by family are: IE-Baltic shows small positive effects (mBERT-L₂ ~2, XLM-L₂ ~1, mBERT-R₂ ~3, XLM-R₂ ~3, mBERT-B₂ ~6, XLM-B₂ ~5); IE-Germanic shows mid-range values for the L₂ bars (~9–10), near-zero to slightly negative values for the R₂ bars (around 0 to about −1), and higher B₂ bars (~15 for both pink and red); IE-Indic shows near-zero L₂ bars (~0–1) and larger R₂ and B₂ bars (mBERT-R₂ ~20, XLM-R₂ ~18, mBERT-B₂ ~24, XLM-B₂ ~21); IE-Romance shows moderate L₂ and mBERT-R₂ bars (~4–6), a small XLM-R₂ bar (~1), and B₂ bars around ~12–13 (mBERT-B₂) and ~6 (XLM-B₂); IE-Slavic shows L₂ bars around ~9–11, R₂ bars near ~0–1, and B₂ bars around ~15–17; IE-other shows L₂ bars near ~6, R₂ bars near ~0, and B₂ bars around ~8; Isolate shows values clustered near zero with small positive R₂ and B₂ bars (roughly ~1–2); Semitic shows positive L₂ and B₂ bars (mBERT-L₂ ~11, XLM-L₂ ~16, mBERT-B₂ ~15, XLM-B₂ ~19–20) alongside negative R₂ bars (around −2 to −1), and it also displays some of the largest error bars; Uralic shows all bars near zero with small positives (generally ~0.5–2). The bars are not presented as a sorted ranking; instead, the category order appears fixed by family naming, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond the consistent use of color and the presence of black error bars with caps.
